raw_responses.Bulgarian:

The outer ring contains eight segments under “Virtual Characters,” each labeled and colored in light blue: “Comic Characters,” “Movie Characters,” “Teleplay Characters,” “Novel Characters,” and “Game Characters,” along with two unlabeled segments that appear to be part of the same group. The inner ring contains “Custom Characters” in pink and “Real Characters” in green. The “Real Characters” segment is further subdivided into six smaller segments in varying shades of green: “Scientists,” “Artists,” “Athletes,” “Writers,” “Musicians,” “Actors,” and “Influencers.” No numerical percentages are displayed on the chart, and there is no explicit legend; however, color coding distinguishes the main categories. The segments appear to be arranged radially without a clear size-based ordering, and no segment is visually emphasized through separation or thickness. The chart uses a clean, minimal design with text labels placed adjacent to or within each segment.

raw_responses.English:
This donut chart visually categorizes character types into two main groups—Virtual Characters and Real Characters—with Virtual Characters occupying the majority of the chart and subdivided into six distinct categories: Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, Game Characters, and Custom Characters, each represented by a light blue segment of varying size. The Real Characters group, shown in green, is further divided into seven subcategories: Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers, each labeled and colored in shades of green. The chart uses a central white circle to form the donut shape, and all segments are labeled directly adjacent to their respective slices without a separate legend. The Virtual Characters section is visually dominant, with its segments arranged clockwise around the chart, while the Real Characters segments are clustered together on the right side. No percentage values are displayed within the slices, and no segments are exploded or emphasized through offsetting or bolding; the relative sizes of the slices suggest proportional distribution, with Comic Characters and Game Characters appearing as the largest virtual subcategories, and Influencers and Actors as the largest real subcategories.
